content.text: I reviewed the full package — brief, conversation, disclosure, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs — and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and dependent claims 2-12, 14-17, 19-22), every one of the 27 entries in draft/numerals.md, every numbered part and relationship in the Field, Summary, Brief Description of Drawings, and Detailed Description, and all seven figure briefs (FIG. 1-7) back to affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md. input/conversation.md is a truncated duplicate of the first four disclosure paragraphs and adds no independent matter; nothing in the draft depends on it. Every core limitation has an exact source anchor: elongated straight rail with flat lower face and upper face; straight longitudinal slot through the rail; printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end with a downwardly projecting portion perpendicular to the rail so the rail extends inward; two screws in two corresponding holes and the reverse-and-reinstall operation moving the projecting portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite side with the same marked upper face used from either edge; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate carriages on the upper face, each with a lower key in the slot that blocks rotation while allowing sliding; one cylindrical bushing per carriage with a vertical bore through the carriage registering with the slot; bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail with a shank through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below, clamping the rail between carriage and shoe; per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and read against the distance marks, whose difference is the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the rail midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the full use sequence; the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list (rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers, knobs); hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitation. Close calls I resolved as entailed rather than untraced, with reasoning: claim 8 and the "same reading direction" statements follow necessarily because only the fence is inverted and the rail and its printed marks are never moved; claim 9/17 and the corresponding description sentence ("received ... as a separate piece that is withdrawable") is the physical content of the disclosed "replaceable wear parts"; claim 12's shoe bearing on and releasing from the lower face is the content of "clamps the rail between the carriage and the shoe" plus "loosening the knob allows the carriage to slide"; claim 22 and "held ... by hand during the drilling" follow from the disclosed "reusable hand tool" that leaves no part attached; and the "slid along the workpiece edge" step is the only way to perform the disclosed alignment of notch and index with the pencil centerline while the fence stays pressed to the edge. I also tested the fence geometry across figures: FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 place projecting portion 32 at the first end bearing on workpiece edge 92 (traced to "the fence is perpendicular to the rail, so the rail extends inward across the workpiece when the fence bears against the edge"), while FIG. 6 shows it standing on one longitudinal side (traced to the reversal passage); these coexist for a transverse fence plate wider than the rail whose lip lies beyond one longitudinal side, so I found no verified contradiction to report. Figure-brief shape choices are confined to the figure briefs and are depiction conventions for affirmatively disclosed parts, each marked "shown schematically": plain block carriages, plain rectangular fence, flat spacer plate, plain round bodies for the knobs, straight elongated slot opening. No figure brief adds depth, taper, angle, runout, radial or circumferential position, contact topology, proportion, or material beyond the source; the V-notch is described only as "shallow V-shaped ... formed in the second end ... aligned with the transverse center index", which is verbatim source substance. No application text says an outline is shown "by way of example" or that a member may have any outline, so no renderer-justifying embodiment was added. Internal consistency checks all pass: each of the 27 numerals denotes exactly one part in the ledger, description, and figure lists, and every ledger numeral appears in at least one figure; every parenthetical figure cite in the description (14/FIG. 4; 12/FIG. 3; 16, 18/FIG. 2; 52, 54, 58, 60/FIG. 5; 72, 74, 78, 80/FIG. 3; 34, 36/FIG. 6; 24, 26, 94/FIG. 7; 40/FIG. 4) matches that figure's numeral list; both section lines carry the same repeated designation at both endpoints in the FIG. 2 brief and are named identically in the Brief Description of Drawings, in the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 brief headings, and in the Detailed Description, with line 3-3 through second carriage 70 and line 5-5 through first carriage 50 consistently everywhere; claims and description use the same relationships and the brief's preserved terminology (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch); antecedent basis holds in every dependent claim; and formalities match the brief (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research statement, apparatus and method claims, no means-plus-function language, abstract about 140 words in a single paragraph). No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any section or figure brief. Background prior-art characterizations were not required to trace to the inventor and were not counted against fidelity. I found no untraced technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency, so the findings array is empty.
